acceptance_evidence: CCA verdict and MergeGate evidence are recorded before completion.
completion_conditions: docs/adr/0016 and docs/adr/0017 exist on the default branch with their content unchanged.
A test fails when any `ADR NNNN` cited in scripts/ has no corresponding docs/adr/NNNN-*.md.
The full suite and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: Measured: `git cat-file -e origin/main:docs/adr/0016-locks-bound-product-paths.md` and the 0017 equivalent both fail; `git ls-tree origin/main docs/adr/` lists 0001-0015 plus README and template. The commits that authored them (9914d22, 9515998) are NOT reachable from origin/main — they were written on a coordinator branch and never rode a PR.

Measured citations on origin/main: `scripts/mergegate_check.py` contains 'ADR 0017' nine times; `scripts/guardian_approval_signal.py` contains 'ADR 0016'/'ADR 0017' seven times. `docs/agents/checklists.md`, `docs/agents/decision-control.md`, `CONTEXT.md` and `AGENTS.md` cite neither.

Why it stayed silent: nothing binds a citation to a file. `grep -n 'docs/adr' scripts/validate_shiki.py` returns nothing — no validator requires a cited ADR to exist. This is the same unbound-pair shape that produced the other silent failures this week, so the fix is the pair binding, not just the two files.

The content is not authored here. Both documents already exist verbatim in the coordinator checkout with their own commit history; this task carries them unchanged. Rewriting a decision record after the fact would misrepresent when the decision was made.

LOCK-SUFFICIENCY CHECK. The two ADR paths are MUST-CHANGE (they are the deliverable). `tests/test_adr_references.py` is MUST-CHANGE (new). Nothing else: `tests/test_install_completeness.py`'s `classify()` returns None for `tests/…` so no TEMPLATE_PATHS entry is needed; `docs/adr/` ships as part of `docs` and needs no manifest change; `scripts/validate_shiki.py` is deliberately NOT locked because the binding lives in a test, not in the validator, and touching validate_shiki would collide with four other backlog items.

Risk is low and honest: no product behaviour changes, no gate moves, no schema changes. Two documents are added and one test asserts a property that already holds once they are. Under `.shiki/guardian-policy.json` (`applies_to_risk: [high, critical]`) neither the Contract PR nor the implementation PR triggers the Guardian gate, so this goal costs zero operator approvals.

non_goals: Rewriting, renumbering or editing the content of either ADR.
Changing scripts/validate_shiki.py, or any gate, schema or workflow.
Fixing any citation in prose docs — none cite these ADRs.
Touching any file outside the declared locks.
outcome: Every `ADR NNNN` a script cites resolves to a real document in the repository. Today two do not: `scripts/mergegate_check.py` cites ADR 0017 nine times and `scripts/guardian_approval_signal.py` cites 0016/0017 seven times, while `docs/adr/` on the default branch stops at 0015. ADR 0017 is the stated basis of the bookkeeping-closeout exemption that has merged seven PRs with zero approvals — its rationale is currently unreadable to anyone auditing that behaviour, human or CCA.
title: Carry the two ADRs the code already cites, and bind citations to files
